pr_title: Use invariant culture when formatting capture transfer in regex source generator
pr_body:
A balancing group can result in TransferCapture being emitted with a negative "capnum". If the compiler is running under a culture that uses something other than '-' as the negative sign, the resulting generated code will fail to compile.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/113077

issue_context.title: error CS1056: Unexpected character '−' with Regex on Mac
issue_context.body:
### Description

Compilation error CS1056 on Mac when using `GeneratedRegex` with this regular expression:

```
[GeneratedRegex("(?>'[^']*'|\"[^\"]*\"|\\([^()]*(((?<open>\\()[^()]*)+((?<-open>\\))[^()]*)+)*(?(open)(?!))\\)|[^'\",])+", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.Compiled, "en")]
```

### Reproduction Steps

On MacOS (Sonoma 14.4) with dotnet 9.0.200, create a minimal project and compile with `dotnet build`:

```csharp
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;

namespace ConsoleApp1
{
    internal partial class Program
    {
        [GeneratedRegex("(?>'[^']*'|\"[^\"]*\"|\\([^()]*(((?<open>\\()[^()]*)+((?<-open>\\))[^()]*)+)*(?(open)(?!))\\)|[^'\",])+", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.Compiled, "en")]
        private static partial Regex FindColumnsPattern();
        static void Main(string[] args)
        {
            Console.WriteLine("Hello World!");
        }
    }
}
```

### Expected behavior

The program compiles

### Actual behavior

The program does not compile and got this error

```
ConsoleApp1 failed with 1 error(s) (0,1s)
    /Users/carlos.saito/tmp/weird-regex/ConsoleApp1/obj/Debug/net9.0/System.Text.RegularExpressions.Generator/System.Text.RegularExpressions.Generator.RegexGenerator/RegexGenerator.g.cs(409,78): error CS1056: Unexpected character '−'
```

Note: in the console message, the `−` in _Unexpected character '−'_ is a [minus sign](https://www.compart.com/en/unicode/U+2212) which is not present in the source code

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

Removing the `-` in the regex capture group compiles, but it is a different expression:

```diff
- [GeneratedRegex("(?>'[^']*'|\"[^\"]*\"|\\([^()]*(((?<open>\\()[^()]*)+((?<-open>\\))[^()]*)+)*(?(open)(?!))\\)|[^'\",])+", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.Compiled, "en")]
+ [GeneratedRegex("(?>'[^']*'|\"[^\"]*\"|\\([^()]*(((?<open>\\()[^()]*)+((?<open>\\))[^()]*)+)*(?(open)(?!))\\)|[^'\",])+", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.Compiled, "en")]
                                                                            ^ here
```

### Configuration

```
$ dotnet --version
9.0.200
```

```
$ dotnet sdk check
.NET SDKs:
Version      Status     
------------------------
9.0.200      Up to date.

.NET Runtimes:
Name                          Version      Status     
------------------------------------------------------
Microsoft.AspNetCore.App      9.0.2        Up to date.
Microsoft.NETCore.App         9.0.2        Up to date.
```

Running on Mac OS 14.4

### Other information

_No response_

The failing generated line is:
```csharp
base.TransferCapture(-1, 4, capture_starting_pos4, pos);
```

That line gets emitted by the regex generator here:
```csharp
writer.WriteLine($"base.TransferCapture({capnum}, {uncapnum}, {startingPos}, pos);");
```
where `capnum` is an integer, that in this case will be -1.

If you just run a simple console app and print out CultureInfo.CurrentCulture and then also CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.NumberFormatInfo.NegativeSign, what do you get? I'm guessing your default culture uses 0x2212 as the negative sign.

We can fix the source generator to always use invariant culture for this, but you can also workaround it by ensuring the compiler is running under a different culture.

review_comments: The generator needs to work on netstandard2.0.
